Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

charts.title: Strict Cash vs Total Liquidity
charts.annotation: Add Cash & equivalents to whichever of the other three bars is populated for that period (J-GAAP periods: + Cash & deposits + Short-term securities; IFRS periods FY2024 on: + Other current financial assets) for total liquidity -- the lines are sequential, not simultaneous.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For INPEX CORPORATION: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For INPEX CORPORATION: this line alone understates real liquidity -- it is the strict cash-flow-statement definition. See the Strict Cash vs Total Liquidity chart below for the fuller picture before judging leverage off this one.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

liquidity.title: Strict cash vs total liquidity
liquidity.content:
Cash & equivalents is the narrow cash-flow-statement definition: cash and instruments maturing within roughly three months. INPEX also holds substantial time deposits and securities beyond three months, which IFRS classifies as current financial assets rather than cash -- these do not show up in the strict line at all.

For INPEX CORPORATION: the gap is large and persistent. FY2016 shows just ¥53.8bn of strict cash against ¥772.5bn of cash & deposits -- fifteen times more. From FY2024 (the IFRS switch), the same broader deposits/securities are reported as Other current financial assets, which reached ¥744bn at H1 FY2026 -- several hundred billion yen above the strict cash balance, held partly as a reserve for the Abadi LNG project. Reading only Cash & equivalents makes INPEX look far more leveraged than it actually is.

What to watch:

  • Total liquidity (strict cash + whichever of the other bars is populated that period) against total debt, not strict cash alone
  • Whether the broader balance is earmarked for a specific project (e.g. Abadi LNG) versus freely available
  • The reporting-basis switch at FY2024: J-GAAP's Cash & deposits / Short-term securities give way to IFRS's single Other current financial assets line

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For INPEX CORPORATION: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For INPEX CORPORATION: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For INPEX CORPORATION: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For INPEX CORPORATION: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For INPEX CORPORATION: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For INPEX CORPORATION: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For INPEX CORPORATION: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For INPEX CORPORATION: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
